summary: In this story, a class buries a time capsule filled with letters and small objects, to be dug up and opened again ten years later.
introduce: Show the title “The Time Capsule” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: to say what you think will happen before it happens
to keep something safe so it lasts a long time

challengeTerms.def: to expect something or prepare for it before it happens
something passed down or left behind for people in the future
people who will be born in the future, especially later generations

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that it is worth the effort to write a letter to your future self? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain why the class decided to make a time capsule and how they prepared it.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review decade, predict, and preserve, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses anticipate, legacy, and posterity to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
